voice: Male, about fifty, British English accent, a rich, warm baritone that stays deep even when he raises his voice; a seasoned radio and television cricket commentator speaking close to a broadcast microphone.

styles.urgent: He erupts with sudden, urgent, high-energy projection on the opening call, his voice lifting and ringing out over a roaring crowd, then pours out the rest at a quick, thrilled pace, still loud.
styles.alarm: A sudden gasp of alarm with high energy, his voice rising sharply, then rushing on breathlessly, loud and urgent, as the ball drops just short of the fielder.
styles.beaten: A sharp, lifted exclamation of surprise, then lively, admiring description at a brisk pace.
styles.poise: Warm, dry and analytical: calm and unhurried, quietly appreciative, a measured conversational pace, low and relaxed, with a hint of a smile.

bowled.text: Right through the gate, off stump out of the ground, timber everywhere!

bowled-yorker.text: Toe-crushing yorker right on the fourth-stump line!

edged-caught.text: Thin feather outside off, swallowed cleanly in the slips!

edged-short.text: Ooh, thick outside edge, drops agonizingly short of second slip!

left-alone.text: Shouldered arms, judged to perfection on the fourth-stump line, watches it carry through.

left-alone-bouncer.text: Sways out of the road, sharp bumper in the corridor, well left alone.

middled.text: Right behind the line, crisp, authoritative forward defensive into the covers.

play-and-miss.text: Lovely shape away off the seam, squared him up, past the outside edge.
